review.algorithm_assessment: Expand each closed axis-aligned track into its positions at integer times during one period. By the generalized Chinese remainder theorem, a position at time i in the first period and time j in the second can occur simultaneously exactly when i and j agree modulo gcd(period1,period2). This includes time zero because the same pair recurs at a positive common period. Group by that residue and find the minimum squared Euclidean distance between the two point sets. A bounding-box KD tree prunes only when its exact integer distance lower bound is no better than the current global best, so the geometric search is exact, not approximate. Repeated coordinates can be deduplicated within a residue. Take a square root only when formatting the final two-decimal result.
